text: The rule is the third party doctrine, built on two 1970s cases about bank records and dialed phone numbers.
provenance: In the 1970s, the Supreme Court decided a pair of cases about information people had handed to someone else — bank records in one, the phone numbers a person dialed in another

text: Once information was handed to a bank or a phone company, the reasonable expectation of privacy in it was gone.
provenance: The Court's logic was that once you voluntarily give information to a third party — a bank, a phone company — you have given up your reasonable expectation of privacy in it. You took the risk that they might turn it over
